text:
Ivy Chen: Proposal — add session-scoped saved queries that auto-expire (default 24h). Use case: quick ad-hoc A/B of filters across routes/models without polluting team library.
Samir Patel: +1. API-wise we should add `scope` enum (session|route|org) and `ttl_seconds`. UX needs a tiny badge 'Ephemeral' + expiry tooltip.
Riley Nguyen: Implementation note: do we keep session state client-only or server-side? Client-only means no sharable link, server-side needs eviction and telemetry. I vote server-side TTL (so we can share/snapshot).
Marta Lopez: Typical users: SRE incident triage, product QA, rollout checks. Also need a cost preview (estimated tokens) when executing ephemeral queries so people don't accidentally spike spend while debugging.
Samir Patel: Telemetry requirements: tag saved_query with `scope`, `created_by`, `expires_at`, `route_filters`, and `sample_rate` if used for telemetry rollups. Also: running these in a shared dashboard should still record API usage against route/model quotas.
Riley Nguyen: Draft API example:
```
POST /api/saved_queries
{
  "name":"session - quick diff",
  "scope":"session",
  "ttl_seconds":86400,
  "filters":[{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"redwood-base-v1","latency":"<150"}],
  "shareable":false
}
```
Samir Patel: Nice. Edge: what happens if someone tries to pin an ephemeral save to org scope? We should provide a "Make persistent" action that copies and converts the scope.
deploy-bot: Heads up — branch `saved-queries-ttl` scheduled to deploy to staging 2026-04-01T03:00Z :rocket:
Ivy Chen: UX specifics — show a small clock icon + relative expiry (e.g., "expires in 23h") on list items, and in the saved-query flyout show 'Convert to persistent' CTA. For share links, add a short-lived token so links stop working after expiry.
Marta Lopez: Alerts & exports question: if a session-scope query is attached to an alert or export job, should we block? I think block and require conversion to org scope to create durable alert. Otherwise parents get stale references.
Samir Patel: Quotas: ephemeral saves shouldn't count toward org saved-query library limits, but we should cap number of active ephemeral saves per user (e.g., 25) to avoid abuse. Executions still count against API/model quotas.
Riley Nguyen: Backend plan: store ephemeral metadata in Redis with TTL for fast eviction and a tombstone in primary DB if converted to org. Emit events: `saved_query.create`, `saved_query.execute`, `saved_query.expire` with route/model tags for telemetry. Also ensure cleanup job for failed TTLs.
Marta Lopez: Decision: proceed with server-side TTL, ephemeral badge UX, API contract above. I'll write a short PRD and wireframes. Owners: Riley (eng), Samir (backend API), Ivy (UX). ETA: 2 sprints.
Samir Patel: I'll add telemetry and quota changes to the backend design doc. Will also include sample rate tagging for any saved query-based evals.
Ivy Chen: UX follow-ups: add hover state that shows exact expiry timestamp, and an option in settings to change default TTL (admins only).
Riley Nguyen: Implementation checklist added to the ticket: API schema, Redis TTL store, DB tombstones, telemetry events, UI badge + convert flow, link token expiry.
Marta Lopez: Sounds good — once PRD is up I'll schedule a sync. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: :eyes:
Ivy Chen: Thanks all — moving this to the roadmap board.
__notes: Thread covers session-scoped ephemeral saved queries, API contract, UX affordances, telemetry, quotas, and implementation plan. Messages are chronological and Slack-style.
